challenger.q: What sort of man did Gladys say she could love?
options: A man of great deeds and strange experiences
challenger.evidence: But, above all, he must be a man who could do, who could act, who could look Death in the face and have no fear of him, a man of great deeds and strange experiences.
challenger.hint: Look again at Malone’s talk with Gladys.

challenger.q: Why did the editor, McArdle, send Malone to Professor Challenger?
options: To try his luck getting a story from him
challenger.evidence: “So why should you not try your luck with Professor Challenger, of Enmore Park?”
challenger.hint: Look again at the newspaper office.

challenger.q: Challenger showed Malone the sketchbook of Maple White. Why was it so important?
options: It had a picture of a creature sketched from the life
It had a map of London
challenger.evidence: That is actually sketched from the life.”

meeting.q: Who was the tall, thin professor who doubted Challenger?
meeting.evidence: Summerlee, the veteran Professor of Comparative Anatomy, rose among the audience, a tall, thin, bitter man

options: By a committee chosen from the audience
meeting.evidence: would be prepared to give it with proper precautions to a committee chosen from the audience.
meeting.hint: Look again at what Challenger says.

meeting.q: Summerlee says claims about the Thames can be tested, but claims about the Amazon cannot. What is his point?
options: Nobody can check a story from somewhere so far away
He has been to the Amazon
meeting.evidence: any assertion about the former could be tested, while about the latter it could not.

amazon.q: Why did they put one professor in each canoe?
options: To keep the peace between them
amazon.evidence: taking the obvious precaution in the interests of peace of putting one Professor into each canoe.
amazon.hint: Look again at how they set off.

amazon.q: Summerlee thinks the trip is a wild-goose chase. Why come along at all?

plateau.q: What grew on top of the rock pinnacle?
plateau.evidence: On the summit of it there grew one high tree.

plateau.q: Why did they need a bridge?
options: A gap lay between the pinnacle and the plateau
plateau.evidence: A drawbridge had to be found which could be dropped across the abyss.
plateau.hint: Look again at the top of the pinnacle.

plateau.q: “The bridge was gone!” Why was that so serious?
options: They were stuck on the plateau with no way back
They had to build another tree
plateau.hint: Think about how they got across.

pterodactyls.q: What did the explorers find in the swamp?
pterodactyls.evidence: The place was a rookery of pterodactyls.

pterodactyls.q: What did the explorers see in a glade, the same day?
pterodactyls.evidence: August the twenty-eighth—the day we saw five live iguanodons in a glade of Maple White Land.
pterodactyls.hint: Look again at the start of the chapter.

pterodactyls.q: Why was it so hard to back away from the pterodactyls?
options: They circled closer whenever the explorers tried to retreat
pterodactyls.evidence: The moment we attempted to retreat the circle closed in upon us
pterodactyls.hint: Look again at the flock in the air.

iguanodons.q: What colour were most of the plateau’s flowers?
iguanodons.evidence: all that morning we wandered among lovely flowers—mostly, as I observed, white or yellow in color
iguanodons.hint: Look again at the morning walk.

iguanodons.q: Why did Malone climb the great tree?
options: To see the plateau and help make a chart of it
iguanodons.evidence: I absolutely refuse to leave, however, until we have made at least a superficial examination of this country, and are able to take back with us something in the nature of a chart.”
iguanodons.hint: Look again at the evening discussion.

iguanodons.q: Malone says he was a skilled tree-climber as a lad. How did that help the team?
options: He could do something useful that the others could not
iguanodons.evidence: Now, ever since I ran wild as a lad in Ireland I have been a bold and skilled tree-climber.
iguanodons.hint: Think about what the chart needed.

captured.evidence: I gave a cry of joy as in the cold gray light I saw Lord John Roxton kneeling beside me.
captured.hint: Look again at the morning after Malone’s night alone.

options: He wanted to bring back a record of the central lake
captured.evidence: suppose I made my way down to the central lake, suppose I was back at breakfast with some record of the place
captured.hint: Look again at the start of the chapter.

captured.q: The chief of the ape-men looked like a red Challenger. Why did Summerlee laugh till he cried?
options: The likeness to Challenger was very funny, even in danger
He was not afraid at all
captured.evidence: This old ape-man—he was their chief—was a sort of red Challenger, with every one of our friend’s beauty points, only just a trifle more so.
captured.hint: Look again at Lord John’s story.
